new_value: Authenticated DAO origination now fails closed on missing/corrupt TX recovery independent of legacy flags, verified end to end. DaoManager._restore_tx_state already retains a terminal _tx_recovery_error whenever origin_identity is configured (independent of require_crash_safety) and validates restored state (canonical DAO byte roundtrip, DODAG context, Origin Sequence match, Schnorr48 transcript) before transmit — verified, no dao_manager changes needed (grep confirmed dao_manager is the only caller of load/store_tx_state). The remaining silent-reset hole was persistence-level and is closed by the cshj marker validation: with a stateless anchor record, deleted TX slots + pre-existing marker now raise at load AND at the crash-safe store commit, so build_dao can neither re-originate from sequence 1 nor silently rebuild deleted slot state; corrupt slots raise 'refusing to overwrite corrupt' (cycr). New manager-level regressions: parametrized delete/corrupt damage with require_crash_safety=False and a stateless anchor -> build_dao raises DaoError(persistence_corrupt) and the failure is terminal on repeat; mid-session store after slot deletion fails closed (verified to fail against pre-cshj code); control test proves explicitly authorized first bootstrap on a genuinely fresh store still originates sequence 1 then 2. Note: _require_authenticated_origination already rejects fail_closed=False backends outright for public origination, so the marker-backed detection operates on fail_closed=True backends.
